author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read ThreatDown Nebula and OneView detections in CEF, which a Windows endpoint picked as the syslog communication endpoint sends to the data collector over TCP or UDP. Malware, PUP, PUM and Ransomware detections go to Antivirus; EDR Suspicious Activity, Exploit, Remote Intrusion and Website detections go to the third-party alert schema.
notes:
Setup:
- In Nebula or OneView, go to Settings > Syslog Logging, pick a Windows endpoint as the syslog communication endpoint, and point it at the data collector over TCP or UDP (TLS isn't offered).

Field mapping:
- Malware, PUP, PUM and Ransomware detections go to Antivirus; EDR Suspicious Activity, Exploit, Remote Intrusion and Website detections go to the third-party alert schema.
- Category names and their short forms (arw, ae, rid, mwac) both work.
- Hashes are read from msg.
- Only Suspicious Activity has a per-event severity (cs2); the header severity is one fixed setting, so other alerts get HIGH, or MEDIUM for websites.

Time:
- The event time is rt, the detection time, because the endpoint polls the console every few minutes and buffers up to 24 hours.

Made up in the samples:
- ThreatDown publishes no example line for Remote Intrusion, Exploit, Ransomware or Suspicious Activity, so those samples follow the documented field table.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 the engine kept CEF's \n escape in msg as two characters, so the parsers accept both forms, and it also stored event_type and sensor_version on the antivirus records, fields its antivirus schema has but the docs' table doesn't list.
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in that lab tenant on 2026-10-13, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser in that tenant matched these lines.
